input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the walk over exc.__cause__ has no cycle guard, so a chain that loops back on itself never reaches None
- failure path: an exception raised with `raise e from e`, or two exceptions that cause each other, makes retry_if_exception_cause_type spin forever at full CPU; the stop conditions never run and the caller hangs

Reviewer finding
- description: The cycle guard on the walk over the exception __cause__ chain was removed, so a cyclic chain makes the while loop spin forever when no cause matches exception_cause_types.
- rationale: Trigger: a retried function raises an exception whose __cause__ chain loops back on itself (e.g. e1.__cause__ = e2 and e2.__cause__ = e1 set manually) and no exception in the chain is an instance of the configured cause types. The loop then never reaches None and never breaks, because the removed seen-set was the only termination guard for cycles. Impact: the retry decision hangs the calling thread instead of returning False and propagating the error.
critique: Both describe the same defect: the walk over the __cause__ chain has no cycle guard, so a self-referential or mutual cause chain never reaches None and the loop spins forever, hanging the caller. The finding's qualifier that no cause matches only says when the infinite loop happens. It is the same mechanism.
